Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

since preposition

from a time until now

also ever since, since childhood, since morning, since then, from (a time)

classical

Ter. Ad. 48: ēdūxī ā parvulō
Cic. Sen. 19: cujus ā morte tertius hic et trīcēsimus annus est

ā, ab + abl.

preposition with the ablative

since, from (a time, an age)

Of a time or a time of life: ā puerō, ā parvulō, since childhood; stronger, jam inde ā. What has lasted until now takes the present tense with jam: jam dūdum animus est in patinīs, my mind has been on the dishes for ages.

Other words

  • ex + abl. — since, from (a point in time)

    preposition with the ablative · also used · classical · Liv. 26.19.5: ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit

    ex eō tempore, since then; ex quō, since the time when.

Examples

  • Ēdūxī ā parvulō; habuī, amāvī prō meō

    I brought him up from when he was tiny; I kept him and loved him as my ownTer. Ad. 48

  • nam mihi magna cum eō jam inde ūsque ā pueritiā fuit semper familiāritās

    for he and I have always been close friends, ever since we were boysTer. Heaut. 183–184

  • cujus ā morte tertius hic et trīcēsimus annus est

    this is the thirty-third year since his deathCic. Sen. 19

  • ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit nūllō diē prius ūllam pūblicam prīvātamque rem ēgit quam in Capitōlium īret

    from the day he came of age, he never did any business, public or private, without first going up to the CapitolLiv. 26.19.5

  • Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.

    My mind has been on the dishes for ages.Ter. Eun. 816

See also for, until, after, long.
